findings.summary: Clean designed no-op sweep. Per-workflow decisions at 2026-08-25T18:42:56–18:43:00Z: graph-loop 'active run exists' (protected); physics-loop 'latest completed run 32866107906 concluded success; no recovery'; intel-loop / product-loop / runtime-loop / cto-council all 'active run exists' (the runtime entry was repair round 3 = 32885208777, then mid-flight; the cto-council entry was push-triggered run 32885390855, cancelled ~1 min later — see sibling record); product-beta-repair.yml and frontier-research.yml 'no completed run to inspect'. No rerun, no cancellation, zero side effects.

Recovery-coverage boundary observable in this pass (policy, durable in workflow source at pinned head_sha): the watchdog re-runs failed jobs ONLY for (a) runner-shutdown cancellations matched by log regex, (b) explicit SPIDER_TRANSIENT_OX_EXHAUSTED, or (c) OpenCode/Ox presence plus an explicit transient network signature; it refuses blind retry when logs are unreadable ('refusing blind retry') and never touches workflows with an active run. Consequence visible in this very window: a concurrency-cancelled council run with ZERO jobs produces neither signature and empty logs, so it is permanently unrecoverable by this mechanism (sibling record 32885390855). Also extends the 'zero-completed-runs club' observation: product-beta-repair.yml AND frontier-research.yml still had zero completed runs at 18:43Z Aug 25 (+~52 min vs the 17:51Z datapoint already recorded).
